data.narrative: Completed Module 3 'Design Documents & RFCs' learning about lightweight vs heavyweight RFC formats, writing a rate limiting design document following lightweight RFC structure, identifying three dangerous gaps in a flawed design document (missing alternatives, hidden assumptions, vague mitigations), and fixing the document by adding genuine alternatives, moving assumptions to open questions, and rewriting mitigations with concrete action plans.

dimension_scores.observation: Identified three dangerous gaps in flawed design document with specific analysis of why each is dangerous and what impact it would have
dimension_scores.evidence: flawed_doc_analysis.md contains detailed analysis of missing alternatives section, critical assumptions, and vague mitigations

dimension_scores.observation: Wrote lightweight RFC with clear problem statement, proposed approach, genuine alternatives, and specific mitigations
dimension_scores.evidence: rate_limiting_rfc.md is one page with all required sections and specific details

dimension_scores.observation: Wrote design document for senior engineer audience assuming competence not familiarity, with business impact clearly stated
dimension_scores.evidence: rate_limiting_rfc.md includes business impact (customer trust, revenue) and technical details

dimension_scores.observation: Applied lightweight RFC structure with problem before solution, alternatives before decision, risks including do-nothing
dimension_scores.evidence: rate_limiting_rfc.md has 5 sections in logical order

dimension_scores.observation: Fixed vague mitigations to concrete action plans with specific thresholds, procedures, and owners
dimension_scores.evidence: event_pipeline_fixed.md includes specific Datadog alert thresholds and scale-consumers.sh script

strengths: Chose lightweight RFC format with reasoning about getting feedback early before emotional attachment
